name: Cenotaph Verge

stars.name: Cenotaph
stars.notes: Quiet red dwarf prone to slow, predictable flares; its steady dimness makes it a reliable landmark for claim surveyors.

planets.name: First Stone
planets.notes: Tidally locked lava world used only as a navigation benchmark.

planets.name: Slate Mark
planets.notes: Airless rock rich in platinum-group ores; its surface is pocked with test bores from three generations of claim jumpers.

planets.name: Last Rite
planets.notes: Cratered and inert; guild tradition holds that dead prospectors' tags are welded to its highest ridge.

planets.name: Rim Frost
planets.notes: Water-ice world occasionally tapped by rig crews for volatiles.

planets.name: Verge's End
planets.notes: Dim outer sentinel, catalogued but never landed upon.

asteroid_belts.name: The Widow's Ledger
asteroid_belts.notes: The registered mining claim itself: a dense metallic belt worked by guild rigs under rotating shift charters.

stations.name: Claimlight Rig
stations.notes: Bolted habitat and ore-processing head on a hollowed nickel-iron body; crews rotate out every ninety days to keep the flare schedule.

faction_control.notes: An independent miners guild holds the registered claim; corporate scouts are turned away at the belt margin without ceremony.

history: Surveyed twice and abandoned twice before the Free Miners Guild registered the belt as a permanent cooperative claim.
A cave-in forty years ago killed eleven miners; their names are engraved on Slate Mark and recited before every shift rotation.
Guild charter renewals have held for six consecutive decades, making the Verge one of the oldest unbroken claims on the Shelf.
description: A small red sun hangs over five airless worlds, casting everything in a permanent ember dusk. The system's substance lies between the second and third orbits, where the dense metallic shoal of the Widow's Ledger catches the dim light like scattered coins. Nothing here breathes; even the guild rigs feel less inhabited than occupied.

The Free Miners Guild works the belt on charter terms unchanged for decades, hauling refined ore to passing bulk carriers on a schedule as regular as tide tables. Light traffic consists almost entirely of ore haulers, crew rotations, and the occasional supply runner out of Requiem Shelf ports. Outsiders who respect the claim's margins are treated with wary courtesy.

Miners still argue about the sealed drift where the cave-in occurred, which the guild has never reopened despite sensor readings suggesting intact machinery beyond. Newcomers are told the names on Slate Mark protect the living, though no one explains from what. A visitor willing to work a shift may learn more than any freight manifest records.
